body.statement: For a finite recursive semi-Markovian causal graph on \(V\), the Shpitser--Pearl ID recursion terminates and is sound and complete for the interventional distribution \(p\{Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\}\): it returns a finite observed-law expression on every identified input, and otherwise returns a hedge.  The hedge proof supplies two finite binary response-function models with the same observational law and different interventional targets, using the parity construction on the returned pair of rooted confounded forests.

source.verbatim_statement: The algorithm returns either an expression derivable from P or a hedge which witnesses the non-identifiability of the effect.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the introduction on page 1220 of the AAAI paper and checked against Figure 3, Theorems 4--6, and Corollary 2 in the publisher PDF.
